speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens right before you become unresponsive, and how long these episodes typically last? Also, do you have any memory of the event once you regain consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a family history of epilepsy or similar seizure disorders, and have you noticed any specific triggers like stress or lack of sleep? I will also request an EEG to evaluate for abnormal brain wave activity. REQUEST TEST: EEG

text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The temporal lobe spikes and your specific symptoms strongly suggest focal seizures. To better understand the structural cause, I will request a brain MRI. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and EEG findings, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of benign epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes or a similar focal epilepsy syndrome. I will request further neurological imaging to rule out subtle structural causes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste is a classic olfactory aura pointing to temporal lobe epilepsy, not benign rolandic epilepsy. Do you experience any automatic behaviors like lip-smacking or chewing during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any automatic behaviors like lip-smacking, chewing, or picking at your clothes during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: Long-term_Video_EEG

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal long-term video EEG is unusual given the clinical presentation, but the muddy taste aura and automatisms strongly point to focal seizures originating in the temporal lobe. I will request a high-resolution MRI of the brain with epilepsy protocol to look for subtle mesial temporal sclerosis or cortical dysplasia. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_Epilepsy_Protocol

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a muddy taste aura, facial grimacing, and post-ictal confusion is classic for temporal lobe epilepsy, even with normal structural imaging. I will request a PET scan to look for subtle metabolic abnormalities in the temporal lobes that might explain the seizures. REQUEST TEST: Brain_PET

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and video EEG, we must consider psychogenic non-epileptic seizures, especially with the complex semiology. Do you recall any significant emotional stressors or traumatic events prior to the onset of these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste is a classic gustatory aura indicating focal seizures originating in the mesial temporal lobe, likely due to mesial temporal sclerosis which can sometimes be missed on standard MRI. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
